newsitem.title: USA: Cuba Gooding Jr wins best supporting actor Oscar.
newsitem.headline: Cuba Gooding Jr wins best supporting actor Oscar.

text.p: Cuba Gooding Jr, who made "Show me the money" one of the most memorable movie lines of the year, saw Oscar gold on Monday night when he won the Academy Award for best supporting actor in "Jerry Maguire."

A thrilled Gooding accepted the award and then broke into a frenzied dance onstage that recalled a scene from the film. "I love you all, I love you all, I love you all," Gooding shouted repeatedly as he danced around the stage in the same manner his character, wide receiver Rod Tidwell, had cavorted and pranced uncontrollably around the end zone.
Later, a more subdued Gooding used a sports analogy to explain how he felt after being honoured.

"I play ice hockey and there's nothing better than that beer or Gatorade when you come off the ice," he told reporters backstage. "The only way I can explain that is that it just tastes refreshing, so this feels refreshing."

Gooding's win over more established actors like James Woods in "Ghosts of Mississippi" and William H. Macy of "Fargo" came as little surprise to most people in Hollywood. Starring opposite Tom Cruise as a football star fast passing his prime and desperate to win a lucrative product endorsement, Gooding stole the movie repeatedly, most memorably with his oft-repeated "Show me the money!"

Gooding, whose first professional performance was a break dance during the closing ceremonies of the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, made his film debut in the 1991 film, "Boyz in the Hood." That role won him notice but did not initially bring a lot of work his way and he often complained of the shortage of good parts for African American actors.
"I want to say, 'Hi Denzel and it feels good brother," Gooding said backstage, in a reference to prominent black actor Denzel Washington.
In 1992, Gooding appeared in another Tom Cruise film, "A few Good Men."
